title: Runtime API stability matrix and advisory versioning workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a pragmatic, operational semantic-versioning and advisory workflow for the Redwood serving runtime. Goal is to provide predictable guarantees to hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers about breaking changes, deprecation signals, LTS channel commitments, rollout gates, and upgrade tooling required to make upgrades safer and auditable.

Scope:
- Formalize MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH rules for runtime API, network protocol, and runtime ABI.
- Define LTS channels and minimal support windows for each channel (notice periods and security fixes).
- Standardize in-band deprecation headers, sunset notices, and advisory pages for breaking changes.
- Rollout gate checklist and automation for canaries, compatibility tests, and progressive percentage rollouts.
- Upgrade tooling: runtime-compat-checker, migration helpers, and preflight validation for Dedicated/Private upgrades.

Why now:
Customers (Dedicated and Private) need deterministic upgrade paths. Without clear semantic guarantees and automated tooling, upgrades cause incidents and rollback toil. This policy reduces incidents and supports multi-channel support (stable LTS vs. current).

High-level policy decisions (proposed):
1) Versioning semantics:
   - MAJOR (breaking): Incompatible changes to server request/response contract, wire protocol, KV cache semantics, or persistent disk format. MAJOR may also indicate removal of previously supported behavior.
   - MINOR (non-breaking feature/deprecation): Additive features, new config flags, or deprecation markers that do not change default semantics. MINOR releases may include feature gates that are disabled by default.
   - PATCH (bugfix): Backwards-compatible bug fixes and security patches.
   - Migration window: For any MAJOR release, we will publish a migration guide and provide a 90-day minimum compatibility advisory for Hosted/Dedicated customers and 120 days for Private (on-prem) customers to schedule upgrades unless an imminent security fix forces an earlier mandatory upgrade.

2) LTS channels and commitments:
   - stable-lts: receives critical bug and security patches for 12 months from initial publish date. Breaking changes never land on stable-lts.
   - current: receives full feature releases and non-breaking MINORs; supported for 4 months after last published MINOR.
   - experimental/nightly: runs edge changes; no uptime SLA. Intended for early testing.
   - Channel selection guidance will be included in the Console and Release Notes.

3) In-band deprecation and advisory headers:
   - Responses from runtime will include RFC-compliant headers when behavior is deprecated: "Deprecation: true" and "Sunset: YYYY-MM-DD" (where applicable). We will also add "X-Redwood-Deprecation-Info" with a short token pointing to a public advisory page.
   - For breaking behavior introduced behind flags, add "X-Redwood-Preview-Flags" with enabled-preview list.

4) Rollout gates and automation:
   - Automated compatibility matrix: every release must run the runtime against a matrix of: public API surface tests, internal SDK smoke tests, kv-cache regression suite, and large-token tail latency tests.
   - Canary windows: default 7-day canary with progressive traffic percentages (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%). Canary must be approved by on-call SRE and release owner.
   - Auto-rollback: health signals (error rate > 0.5%, 95th latency regression > 2x baseline, or tail memory OOM trends) trigger automated rollback.

5) Upgrade tooling and developer experience:
   - runtime-compat-checker (CLI): validates a given customer config, model artifact, and common request patterns against a candidate runtime binary to catch incompatible behavior.
   - migration-helper scripts: generate request/response diffs for known deprecation patterns and provide recommended request rewrites.
   - preflight APICheck endpoint for Dedicated/Private: customers can POST a small corpus to a staging endpoint to detect contract breakages before scheduling an upgrade.

Deliverables:
- Formal policy doc (this ticket -> Confluence) with examples and allowed/non-allowed breaking changes.
- Deprecation header and advisory page design + Console integration.
- runtime-compat-checker MVP and CI integration.
- Automated release pipeline gating rules and canary automation playbook.

Operational notes:
- All breaking changes must be discussed at Release Council and recorded in a release advisory.
- For Private customers, we will provide an "upgrade-assist" checkbox that triggers SRE runbooks and a 1:1 pre-upgrade validation call.

Risks:
- Overly permissive MINOR rules could hide customer-impacting changes; tests and canaries mitigate this.
- Customers on old Private installs may lag; need to balance notice periods with security patching cadence.

Success metrics:
- Reduced rollback rate after upgrades by 50% within the next two major cycles.
- 95% of runtime releases pass the compatibility matrix with zero manual fixes.
- Customer satisfaction score for Dedicated upgrades > 8/10 on post-upgrade surveys.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc published to Confluence and linked from release notes
Deprecation headers implemented in runtime responses and validated by integration tests
runtime-compat-checker CLI available in CI for all release branches
Canary automation integrated into pipeline with auto-rollback thresholds configured
Migration guide template created and included in every MAJOR release advisory
notes: Decided to use RFC-style 'Deprecation' and 'Sunset' headers rather than custom-only headers to maximize compatibility.
For Private customers, extend migration window to 120 days due to slower change control processes.
We will not backport MINOR non-breaking features to stable-lts; only PATCH security/bug fixes are backported.
